06b_1_boost_hyperbolas.png: A boost of the frame in the plane of the time $x4$ and the hidden direction $x0$. The boosted frame directions $e'^{(x4)} = \cosh b\, e^{(x4)} + \sinh b\, e^{(x0)}$ (blue arrows) and $e'^{(x0)} = \sinh b\, e^{(x4)} + \cosh b\, e^{(x0)}$ (orange arrows) for the rapidities $b = 0, 0.5, 1$ (fainter for larger $b$), drawn with their $x4$ component $t$ horizontally and their $x0$ component $y$ vertically (pure numbers). They move along the unit hyperbolas $t^2 - y^2 = 1$ and $y^2 - t^2 = 1$ and tilt symmetrically towards the light line $t = y$ (dotted).
06b_2_boosted_contraction.png: The contraction $\gamma'^\mu\Omega'_\mu = c_0\gamma^{(x0)} + c_4\gamma^{(x4)}$ in three frames of the same metric, on the history of the Revision record with $H = 1$ ($c_g = \frac32e^{x_4/3}$, $v_g = \frac56$): the coefficient $c_0$ (left) and $c_4$ (right) versus the time $x_4$ in units $1/H$. Solid: no boost, $c_0 = c_g$ and $c_4 = v_g$. Dashed: the constant rapidity rate $b = 3x_4$, which removes the $c_g$ term only at $x_4 = 0$. Dash-dotted: the rapidity $b = 9(e^{x_4/3} - 1)$ with $b' = 2c_g$, which removes it at every time and leaves $v_g(\cosh b\,\gamma^{(x4)} - \sinh b\,\gamma^{(x0)})$: the same metric, a different frame, a different value.
06b_3_boosted_connection_heat_maps.png: The boosted vielbein with the rapidity rate $b' = 2c_g$ at the sample point $H = 1$, $x_4 = 1/2$, $z = \pi/4$, $a_4 = 1/2$, $a_4' = 1$, $b_4 = e^{2/3}$, $b_4'/b_4 = 4/3$ (the history of the Revision record at $a_4 = 1/2$) with the rapidity $b = 9(e^{1/6} - 1) = 1.632$, as 16 x 16 heat maps (red positive, blue negative, white zero; rows and columns are the spinor components; each panel has its own colour scale). Left: $\Omega'_{x4}$, nonzero because the frame turns with time; middle: $\Omega'_{x0}$; right: the contraction $\gamma'^\mu\Omega'_\mu$, which is only the term $v_g(\cosh b\,\gamma^{(x4)} - \sinh b\,\gamma^{(x0)})$: the boost removed the term $c_g\gamma^{(x0)}$.
06b_4_ricci_components.png: The mixed Ricci tensor of the corrected metric, which is diagonal, on the history of the Revision record ($a_4 = x_4$, $b_4 = e^{4x_4/3}$, $H = 1$), in units of $H^2$. Left: the eight components $R^\mu{}_\mu$ at $x_4 = 1/2$ (blue: the hidden direction and the three extra times, which share one value; red: 3-space; gray: time). Right: $R^{x0}{}_{x0} = R^{x5}{}_{x5}$ (solid), $R^{x1}{}_{x1}$ (dashed), $R^{x4}{}_{x4}$ (dotted) and the Ricci scalar $R$ (gray dash-dotted) versus the time $x_4$ in units $1/H$; for the flat member $a_4 = 0$, $b_4 = H^2x_4^2$ of the family every curvature component is zero (black line). The metric is curved on the history.

06b_6_rescaling.png: The rescaling $\Psi = w_r\chi$ with $w_r = e^{a_4/2}b_4^{-1}(\sin^2 z)^{-1/8}$, drawn for $H = 1$ at $a_4 = 0$, $b_4 = 1$. Left: the weight $(\sin^2 z)^{-1/8}$ versus the hidden angle $z$ in radians across one cell (vertical line: the fold). Right: the two terms of the coefficient of $\gamma^{(x0)}\chi$ in the field equation of $\chi$, the derivative term $\partial_{x0}w_r/f_0 = -c_gw_r$ (solid) and the spin-connection term $c_gw_r$ (dashed), in units of $H$, and their sum (dotted), which is zero at every $z$: in the variable $\chi$ the equation has no term $c_g\gamma^{(x0)}$ (and, by the factor $e^{a_4/2}b_4^{-1}$, no term $v_g\gamma^{(x4)}$).
